5 Unusual Tools That Make Fishkeeping Easier! These five aquarium maintenance tools cost very little, but they save me time when cleaning my fish tanks, removing floating plants, feeding fish, and testing aquarium water. First is a toothbrush, and I buy the cheapest ones I can find because I want stiff bristles for scrubbing algae off hardscape. They are useful for getting into awkward corners of aquarium glass and cleaning areas that larger brushes struggle to reach. Keep a new toothbrush just for your aquarium, with no toothpaste or household cleaning products on it. Second is a hair comb for scooping out excess floating plants. It works well with duckweed and Wolffia, but I also use it for Salvinia minima, red root floaters, and Spirodela. Removing excess growth helps stop floating plants covering the entire surface and blocking too much light from reaching the plants underneath. Third are measuring spoons, which I use to portion out fish food. Cheap spice-measuring spoons make it easier to give each aquarium a consistent amount, rather than guessing with a different-sized pinch every day. That consistency makes it easier to adjust feeding, avoid overfeeding, and keep track of the nutrients going into your planted tank. Fourth is a pipette for filling the test tubes in a liquid aquarium water test kit. Because those tubes hold testing chemicals, I prefer to transfer tank water with a dedicated pipette instead of dipping the tubes straight into the aquarium. It also makes topping up to the fill line much easier. Finally, I keep small brushes for cleaning inside the test tubes. These are sold as drain-cleaning brushes in my area: I mean the physical brushes, not drain-cleaning chemicals! They help remove residue that can make the colour readings harder to judge. Use appropriately sized brushes, rinse your equipment thoroughly, and keep everything dedicated to aquarium use. You don't need an expensive maintenance kit to make fishkeeping easier. #aquarium  #fishtank  #fishkeeping
